draft.title: Angle sum of a triangle
card: The three angles inside any triangle add to 180°. This is true for every triangle, whatever its shape or size.
To find a missing angle, add the two angles you know. Then subtract that total from 180°.
Example: a triangle has angles of 50° and 65°. Add them: \(50^{\circ} + 65^{\circ} = 115^{\circ}\). The third angle is \(180^{\circ} - 115^{\circ} = 65^{\circ}\).
A right angle is 90°. If a triangle has a right angle, the other two angles add to 90°.
draft.remember: Add the two known angles, then take the total away from 180°.

a.q: Two angles inside a triangle are 70° and 45°. What size is the third angle?
a.why: \(70^{\circ} + 45^{\circ} = 115^{\circ}\), and \(180^{\circ} - 115^{\circ} = 65^{\circ}\). The answer 115° is wrong because it is only the sum of the two known angles, and the step of subtracting from 180° was skipped.
a.clue: Add the two angles you know, then subtract from 180°.

b.q: Mia cuts a triangle of card in Melbourne. One angle is a right angle and another is 38°. What is the size of the third angle?
b.why: A right angle is 90°, so \(90^{\circ} + 38^{\circ} = 128^{\circ}\). Then \(180^{\circ} - 128^{\circ} = 52^{\circ}\). The answer 142° comes from subtracting 38° from 180° and forgetting the right angle.
b.clue: A right angle is 90°, so use it as one of the known angles.
